It looks like your message ("Dht agq do paln4c xbso4bf3obnthwa99r otcarry ou totsytnehsi") has some typos, and appears to be asking:

**"What gas do plants absorb from the air to carry out photosynthesis?"** (or "What do plants absorb from the air to carry out photosynthesis?")

The answer is **carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$)**. 

During photosynthesis, plants take in **carbon dioxide** from the air (through tiny pores on their leaves called *stomata*) and **water** from the soil, using energy from **sunlight** to convert them into **glucose** (sugar for energy/growth) and releasing **oxygen** ($\text{O}_2$) back into the air:

$$6\text{CO}_2 + 6\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{light energy} \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6 + 6\text{O}_2$$

*(If you meant something else by your message, please clarify!)*
